title: Checkout Item Holder Correction
lede: Staff can now record who actually has each serialized item after a sideline or travel handoff, without splitting the checkout or rewriting its scan history.

stats.n: The serialized line remains on its original checkout
Returned items and closed checkouts stay immutable
Batteries and pooled quantities remain checkout-level custody

sections.heading: Same checkout, corrected holder
sections.note: Same deterministic fixture, asset, checkout, and viewport. Only the committed item-holder assignment changes.

pairs.title: Desktop equipment row
pairs.sub: The explicit holder appears below the asset identity with the canonical avatar treatment.
pairs.beforeCap: The shared manifest carried CAM-104 with no explicit person attached.
pairs.afterCap: Jordan Lee is visibly recorded as the person holding CAM-104.

pairs.title: Narrow equipment row
pairs.sub: The same attribution remains readable at the 390px authenticated mobile-web viewport.
pairs.beforeCap: The item inherited shared checkout custody.
pairs.afterCap: The explicit holder wraps below the item metadata without hiding row actions.

changes.was: A whole checkout could transfer owners, but a camera or lens swapped between people still appeared under the original manifest with no correction path.
changes.now: Staff/Admin can use Assign holder or Change holder on one active serialized row and optionally record handoff context.

changes.h: Correction could not weaken checkout truth
changes.was: Moving equipment between checkouts would risk fragmenting scan, allocation, event, and return history.
changes.now: The mutation changes only assignedUserId/assignedAt, advances the booking snapshot, and writes an audit entry in one serializable transaction.

changes.was: The travel-case workflow deliberately avoided falsely assigning pooled gear to a person.
changes.now: A blank holder still inherits personal-owner or shared-manifest custody; only serialized exceptions are attributed, while bulk gear stays pooled.

verification: 18 focused Vitest checks pass across service, route, stale retry, response shape, UI source, booking freshness, and kiosk-custody boundaries.
Authenticated Playwright passes at desktop and 390px against an isolated Preview-backed local server with deterministic route fixtures and no live booking mutation.
TypeScript and ESLint pass for the current working tree.
notes: The assignment dialog was also captured at desktop and narrow widths in this proof folder and visually inspected.
No Notre Dame production checkout was changed, and this source has not been committed, pushed, or deployed.
My Gear, accountability, reports, native iOS, and kiosk presentation do not yet treat explicit item holders as their primary attribution; that is the next bounded slice under GAP-78.
